ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, senior managers, and authorized signatories against OFAC Special Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Council sanctions lists, UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) sanctions, CIMA Advisory Notices, and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission sanctions. Use continuous automated monitoring; enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, family member, close associate, or politically exposed entity; full CDD documentation is required before incorporation and branch registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands General Registry Online Portal (ciregistry.gov.ky); Gibraltar Companies House Portal (csra.gov.gi) for subsequent foreign company registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Cayman and Gibraltar company names must be expressed in Latin characters (English). No statutory transliteration into Chinese or non-Latin scripts is recognized for the company's official registered name. Trademark-style non-Latin names may appear as a secondary trade name only. Hyphens, numerals, and common typographic symbols are permitted, but the name must be visually distinct and not misleadingly similar to any existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: For Cayman: if a proposed name is rejected, file a 'Request for Reconsideration' with the Registrar of Companies within 21 days of refusal. Extensions are not available beyond the initial 30-day reservation; re-submit with a new fee. For Gibraltar: if the branch name is rejected under section 39(5) Companies Act 2014, file an administrative appeal with the Gibraltar Registrar within 28 days; further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar. Parallel name re-check must be completed before final incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for the Cayman Islands registered office mandate only. For Gibraltar economic substance purposes, a physical office, qualified staff, and decision-management presence are required if the company purports to be tax resident in Gibraltar or claims EU/UK gateway substance. As the business is a medical device OEM (X-ray flat panel detectors), a virtual office alone will not satisfy Gibraltar economic substance rules under the Criminal Justice (Economic Substance) Act 2019.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual inspection likelihood: 30% for Cayman registered office; 40% for Gibraltar registered office; up to 60% if the company claims Gibraltar tax residence or holds a medical device distribution license; unannounced physical inspections may reach 80% if banking relationships are established with regulated Gibraltar banks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2023 Revision), ss. 14-17 (incorporation), ss. 40-47 (exempted companies); Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, Part 21 (overseas companies); Gibraltar Medical Devices Regulations 2021 (regulated manufacturing activity).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Companies Division; Companies House Gibraltar, Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation under section 14 of the Cayman Islands Companies Act; Form FC / Application for Registration as a Foreign Company under Part 21 of the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Cayman exempted company. The board may adopt an authorised capital of USD 50,000 and defer paid-up capital. If subscription funds are contributed before the share register reflects allotment, those funds must be held in a designated client-money escrow account maintained by the licensed corporate services provider and released only against issued share certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as a written resolution of the first directors, that the subscription agreement of the initial subscriber is approved, and that 50,001 management and ordinary shares of USD 0.01 each be issued and allotted to the subscriber in consideration of cash; RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [Cayman registered office address], with [registered office provider] appointed to maintain the registered office; RESOLVED that [Director] be appointed as Director, [Secretary] as Secretary and [Officer] as Compliance Officer; RESOLVED that the Directors are authorised to open bank, escrow and EMI accounts, execute the Gibraltar foreign-company registration, and sign any ancillary statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Companies Division, via an approved registered agent e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Cayman licensed registered agent; draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the Companies Act; complete UBO declarations, AML/KYC forms, and consent of the registered office provider; obtain subscriber approval; notarize where required; reserve the chosen company name with the Registry if a name clearance search is requested.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association signed by the subscriber
Name clearance / availability report from the Cayman Registry
Consent to act as Director
Consent of Registered Office Provider
Passport copies and proof of address of ultimate beneficial owners
AML/KYC questionnaire completed by the introducing incorporated agent
Bank reference letter for the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the name, file a revised availability search and adopt an alternate name; if the M&A is deficient, prepare a short-form amendment and resubmit within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Payment of Government Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Companies Division (Companies Act e-filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration of the exempted company, together with the M&A, Declaration of Compliance, notice of registered office, and statutory consents; pay the Cayman government incorporation fee; receive the Certificate of Incorporation; retain original and certified copies for Gibraltar registration and banking.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Act Form)
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Declaration of Compliance completed by the subscriber and registered agent
Notice of Cayman Registered Office
Name clearance and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete dossiers, deliver a written response and corrected statutory declaration within ten business days; if rejected, appeal by administrative review to the Registrar and thereafter to the Grand Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Governance and Share Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Company Secretary; statutory registers maintained at the Cayman registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass the pro-forma written resolution; approve the share subscription; record allotment in the register of members; appoint the Director, Secretary, and Compliance Officer; open the statutory books; issue share certificates; file the register of directors and directors' interests with the registered office.
required_dossiers: First Board Written Resolution
Subscriber's share subscription payment evidence
Register of Members
Register of Directors and Officers
Share certificates prepared for issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office provider withdraws consent, appoint a replacement Cayman licensed provider and file a change of registered office notice with the Registry within fourteen days; if share issuance contains a defect, cancel and reissue certificates by board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Evidence of Good Standing and Exempted Tax Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry and Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar and, where available, obtain the exemption undertaking confirming that the company may be tax-exempt for twenty years from incorporation; record the exempted status in the company's minute book for Gibraltar filing and financial institution due diligence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Application for Certificate of Good Standing
Annual return and confirmation of paid-up capital data
Copy of Cayman registered office consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Good Standing certificate is delayed due to outstanding annual fees, pay the relevant fee and request expedited issuance; if the tax exemption undertaking is contested, rely on the zero-rated corporate income tax regime of the Cayman Islands and document the statutory basis.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar, Registrar of Companies, HM Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form FC / Application for Registration as a Foreign Company together with certified copies of the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, M&A, Certificate of Good Standing, register of directors and officers, notice of Gibraltar registered office, and consent of the Gibraltar local agent or process agent; pay the Gibraltar filing fee; once registered, display the company name and country of incorporation at any Gibraltar place of business.
required_dossiers: Form FC / Foreign Company Application
Certified copy of Cayman Certificate of Incorporation
Certificate of Good Standing from the Cayman Registrar
Certified Memorandum and Articles of Association
Register of Directors and Company Secretary
Notice of Gibraltar registered office
Consent of Gibraltar corporate service provider / local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused on name similarity grounds, request an alternate registered name or add a distinguishing suffix; if the application is rejected on compliance grounds, submit a corrected pack and pay any restoration fee within twenty-eight days; final appeal lies to the Gibraltar Supreme Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturing Authorisation for Class IIa/IIb X-Ray Diagnostic Detectors (Medical Devices (Gibraltar) Regulations 2021)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Screening) under the Environmental Impact Assessment and Habitats Regulations; full EIA is not required for cleanroom-based amorphous silicon and cesium iodide detector assembly, but full EIA would be triggered if production generates hazardous waste exceeding two tonnes per year or VOC emissions exceed five tonnes per year.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to sewer: pH 6.5-9.5, BOD5 not exceeding 30 mg/L, COD not exceeding 125 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 60 mg/L, and total heavy metals not exceeding 10 mg/L. Air emissions: VOC abatement to not more than 50 mg C/Nm3; cesium iodide deposition chamber exhaust must pass HEPA filtration before discharge; hazardous chemical waste must be consigned to an authorised licensed carrier with full waste consignment notes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire and Rescue Service Act; Building Control structural load approval for cleanroom floor slabs, X-ray shielding, and plant equipment; occupational health and safety workplace clearance issued by the Health and Safety at Work Unit, covering radiation protection, cleanroom contamination control, emergency preparedness, and employee training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (Ministry of Finance, HM Government of Gibraltar), 6-8 Hargreaves Chambers, 311 Main Street, Gibraltar; online filing portal: GO Tax (https://taxoffice.gibraltar.gov.gi); customs administration: Gibraltar Customs and Border Agency (GCBA), Gibraltar Port.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Engage a Gibraltar-licensed corporate services provider (Companies Act 2014, Part 16; FSC licensing regime) to file the foreign-company registration particulars with the Gibraltar Companies Registry, including certified Cayman certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles, and register of directors and members. Step 2: Within 30 days of commencing economic activity, file the corporate tax registration application with the Gibraltar Income Tax Office (GO Tax e-portal), submitting the certified Cayman incorporation documents, beneficial-ownership details (Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2019), and particulars of the appointed Gibraltar resident agent/registered office. Step 3: Obtain the Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN), normally issued in 5-10 business days, and the Customs Reference Number (GRN) from GCBA for import/export clearance. Step 4: If the entity establishes an office, staff, or dependent agent in Gibraltar (creating a permanent establishment under UK/Gibraltar arrangements), register the branch/PE with the Income Tax Office and file annual returns; if no PE exists and no central management-and-control is exercised from Gibraltar, file an annual non-residence declaration to preserve status outside the Gibraltar income tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (the Cayman Exempted Company is tax-exempt in its home jurisdiction under the Cayman Tax Concessions Act; in Gibraltar it is treated as a non-resident foreign company unless managed-and-controlled from Gibraltar, in which case territorial corporate income tax applies at 12.5% on Gibraltar-source and remitted income only, per Income Tax Act 2010, s. 8-16, as amended)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a check-the-box system. Available statutory elections: (i) group-loss surrender election (Income Tax Act 2010, s. 54) for 75%-related companies; (ii) capital-allowances pooling election including the annual investment allowance (GIP 50,000); (iii) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) election on qualifying new equity under the Income Tax (Notional Interest Deduction) Regulations 2019; (iv) residence confirmation election / advance clearance with the Commissioner under the Income Tax (Residence of Companies) Rules 2018; (v) advance pricing arrangement for inter-company royalty and services transactions under the Income Tax Act 2010, s. 76. Hybrid mismatch elections are unavailable: OECD BEPS Action 2 rules are mandatory and automatically re-characterise deductible payments by the Cayman entity to related offshore recipients.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar Import Duty and Excise Regime (Customs Duties Ordinance 1958) - Gibraltar has NO VAT, NO GST, and NO sales/use tax, being excluded from the EU VAT area (1972 Act of Accession, Art. 28) and outside the UK VAT regime post-Brexit
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A - no turnover-based indirect tax registration exists in Gibraltar; importers/exporters must obtain a GRN (Gibraltar Reference Number) from GCBA. For supplies routed through the UK or EU, the Cayman entity must register for UK VAT (currently GBP 90,000 taxable-supplies threshold) or destination EU Member State VAT where distance-selling thresholds (e.g., EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold) are exceeded; domestic medical-device sales are standard-rated (UK 20%) with zero-rating applying only to direct export.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal e-invoicing or Continuous Transaction Controls (CTC) stamping regime applies in Gibraltar. Customs declarations are made electronically through the Gibraltar Electronic Customs System (GECS), interoperable with the UK Customs Declaration Service (CDS); EU-bound exports require an ICS2 ENS filing. E-invoicing (PEPPOL/UBL or UN/CEFACT) is commercially recommended but not statutorily mandated for digital X-ray flat-panel detector transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Gibraltar has no VAT, so export zero-rating arises only where the Cayman entity routes DR flat-panel detectors through the UK/EU supply chain: (i) UK zero-rating under VATA 1994, s. 30(6) and Sch. 8, Group 14 applies to goods physically exported outside the UK within 3 months, conditional on prescribed export evidence; (ii) EU zero-rating under Directive 2006/112/EC, Art. 146 applies to intra-Community dispatches where the customer holds a valid EORI/VAT number; (iii) input VAT suffered in the UK/EU may be recovered by the non-resident Cayman entity under the 13th VAT Directive procedure (Directive 86/560/EEC) or via UK VAT 161A certificate procedures; (iv) exports of HS 9022.14 / 9018.14 X-ray detector panels from Gibraltar attract no Gibraltar export duty and no Gibraltar VAT refund mechanism is available because no input VAT is chargeable in Gibraltar. Zero-rating is denied if export evidence is not secured within the statutory time limits or if goods are subsequently returned to the UK/EU market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (GECS/CDS single administrative declaration with unique movement reference)
Bill of Lading (master and house) or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Gibraltar/UK/EU territory
Commercial Invoice (HS 2017 code 9022.14 or 9018.14; DAP/CIF value; exporter GRN and EORI references)
Packing List with serial numbers for the amorphous-silicon / caesium-iodide flat-panel detectors
Certificate of Origin (UK-Gibraltar export certification, or EUR.1/ATR movement certificate for preferential EU trade)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank FX conversion confirmation from a Gibraltar-licensed bank evidencing receipt and crediting of export proceeds)
Medical Device Export / Free Sale Certificate issued by the Gibraltar Medicines Authority under the Medical Devices Regulations 2021 (CE/UKCA-marked device)
End-User Clinical Installation Certificate (radiology OEM attestation of final installation at a licensed healthcare facility)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Failure to substantiate export within the evidence deadlines triggers: (i) retrospective clawback of UK zero-rating (VATA 1994, s. 36 and s. 73) with statutory interest from the date of supply plus penalties of 30%-100% for deliberate inaccuracies; (ii) Gibraltar Customs Ordinance 1958, s. 178-179, penalties up to GIP 10,000 per false declaration and forfeiture of goods; (iii) Income Tax Act 2010, s. 89-91, a 100% negligence penalty (reducible to 50% on voluntary disclosure) where export proceeds unrepatriated beyond the 180-day deadline are reclassified as unremitted offshore income; (iv) criminal liability for fraudulent evasion of duty/tax, punishable by imprisonment of up to 7 years under the Criminal Procedure (Fraud) Act 2011; (v) asset-freezing and anti-money-laundering enforcement by the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015. The Gibraltar-GB-Cayman Tax Information Exchange Agreement and OECD Common Reporting Standard enable automatic retrospective data exchange among the Gibraltar Income Tax Office, HMRC, and the Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority in cases of suspected export zero-rating fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England anchors the Gibraltar Pound (GIP) framework at a 1:1 parity with GBP; GIP banknotes are legally issued by the Government of Gibraltar through the Commissioner of Currency. The Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the exclusive statutory regulator licensing and supervising all banks, electronic money institutions, and payment service providers in Gibraltar. HM Treasury retains sovereignty oversight over Gibraltar's financial services sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. Gibraltar and the UK impose no exchange controls, no central bank approval for inbound capital injection into a Cayman Exempted Company, and no restriction on outbound dividends, intercompany loan repayments, or profit repatriation to the Cayman shareholder. GIP and GBP circulate at par with unlimited interchangeability; USD, EUR, and GBP multi-currency accounts are standard. Profit remittances are subject to zero Gibraltar withholding tax (dividends, interest, royalties, capital gains), and the Cayman entity itself is tax-exempt under Cayman law. The only material hurdles are bank-level source-of-funds due diligence and OECD international tax compliance (Cayman Economic Substance Notification and CRS reporting).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio to GIP/GBP, and no repatriation deadline under Gibraltar or UK law. Export proceeds from the ISIC 3250 digital X-ray flat panel detector manufacturing business may be held indefinitely in USD, EUR, or GBP, applied toward supplier settlements, or used as collateral for LC and trade finance facilities.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance and Commercial LC Account
